original_question: Is the class of lattices that are isomorphic to a sublattice of the lattice of normal subgroups of some group a variety?
target_in_paper: Section 2, Problem 38 of the notebook: "Is the class of lattices that are isomorphic to a sublattice of the lattice of normal subgroups of some group a variety?"
correct_elements: Your draft is essentially the exact wording of Problem 38 in the paper. It correctly identifies the right class of lattices, uses the paper's 'isomorphic to a sublattice of the lattice of normal subgroups of some group' formulation, and asks the intended meta-question of whether that class forms a variety.
missing_details: Make explicit that this is a question about a class of lattices in the usual lattice signature {∨, ∧}.

Spell out the quantifiers: for a lattice L, there should exist some group G such that L is lattice-isomorphic to a sublattice of N(G), where N(G) is the lattice of normal subgroups of G ordered by inclusion.
Clarify that 'variety' means an equational class of lattices, i.e. a class axiomatizable by a set of lattice identities.
State that no finiteness assumption is imposed on either the lattice L or the group G.
Clarify that 'sublattice' means closed under the meet and join inherited from N(G).

Make clear that the question is about normal subgroup lattices of arbitrary groups, not the neighboring problems in the paper about self-duality, linear lattices, commuting equivalence relations, or subgroup lattices of abelian groups.
refined_question: Let K be the class of all lattices L such that there exists a group G for which L is lattice-isomorphic to a sublattice of N(G), the lattice of normal subgroups of G ordered by inclusion. Is K a variety of lattices; that is, is there a set of lattice identities whose models are exactly the lattices in K?
justification: The draft already matches Problem 38 almost verbatim, so the faithful refinement is only to make the ambient signature, quantifiers, and the meaning of 'variety' explicit. I did not broaden the problem to neighboring questions in the notebook. In particular, although the historical source cited by the notebook (Jonsson 1953, Section 5) phrases a related question using lattices isomorphic to lattices of normal subgroups, the arXiv paper's official formulation for this problem is the sublattice version, so that wording should be preserved. The neighboring Problem 35 and Jonsson's Section 5 show that the intended meaning of asking whether a class is a 'variety' is equational axiomatizability by lattice identities.
